correctness.rationale: From the defining equation \(T_i-T_{n-i}^*T_n=D_{T_n}F_iD_{T_n}\), one gets \(D_{T_n}=\operatorname{diag}(1,s)\) and the triangular formula for \(F_i\). Exact multiplication gives \([F_i,F_j]=-\lambda_n\Delta_{ij}s^{-3}N\) and the mixed-adjoint defect \(\Delta_{ij}s^{-2}\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\). The simultaneous vanishing of all \(\Delta_{ij}\) is exactly a two-row rank-one condition, equivalent to reversal-conjugation up to a unimodular phase. Boundary cases \(n=2\), \(\lambda_n=0\), and the zero row were checked explicitly.

value.rationale: The result converts a one-sided failure construction into a complete structural boundary for a canonical nilpotent slice. It shows that the two dilation conditions are controlled by the same Plücker-type minors when \(\lambda_n\ne0\), identifies the exact degeneration at \(\lambda_n=0\), and replaces a list of coefficient inequalities by a natural reversal-conjugation symmetry up to phase. This is a motivated classification tied directly to the focal paper's central obstruction, not an arbitrary parameter exercise.
